IN NO EVENT SHALL THE COPYRIGHT OWNER OR CONTRIBUTORS BE LIABLE FOR * ANY DIRECT, INDIRECT, INCIDENTAL, SPECIAL, EXEMPLARY, OR CONSEQUENTIAL DAMAGES * (INCLUDING, BUT NOT LIMITED TO, PROCUREMENT OF SUBSTITUTE GOODS OR SERVICES; * LOSS OF USE, DATA, OR PROFITS; OR BUSINESS INTERRUPTION) HOWEVER CAUSED AND * ON ANY THEORY OF LIABILITY, WHETHER IN CONTRACT, STRICT LIABILITY, OR TORT * (INCLUDING NEGLIGENCE OR OTHERWISE) ARISING IN ANY WAY OUT OF THE USE OF THIS * SOFTWARE, EVEN IF ADVISED OF THE POSSIBILITY OF SUCH DAMAGE. */ package com.varlamoredistraction; /** * How urgent a tracked world is, derived purely from seconds elapsed since its last distraction. *

* The bands exist because the next distraction fires 84-99 seconds after the last one. Below the * first threshold the world cannot possibly fire yet, so there is no reason to be standing on it. * {@link #IMMINENT} means it may already have fired unseen. Once past the last threshold it * certainly has, and since we were not there to witness it the new cycle began at an unknown * instant - the counter now carries no information, which is why {@link #MISSED} freezes rather * than rolling over. */ enum DistractionState { /** * The distraction is running right now - 100% success, auto-pickpocketing, and no reason to be * anywhere else. *

* This is the one band whose boundary is deterministic. A distraction ends a fixed interval * after it starts, so the time left in it is a countdown that can be stated exactly; the next * distraction is random across 84-99s and can only be estimated. The panel shows this band as * time remaining rather than time elapsed, because the two numbers mean genuinely different * things and displaying both as a count-up would imply a precision the other bands do not have. */ ACTIVE, /** Plenty of time; safe to be on another world. */ FRESH, /** The window is opening - go now. */ APPROACHING, /** Firing now, or already fired. */ IMMINENT, /** Missed it. Phase is unknown until this world is observed again. */ MISSED }

Redistributions in binary form must reproduce the above copyright notice, * this list of conditions and the following disclaimer in the documentation * and/or other materials provided with the distribution. * * THIS SOFTWARE IS PROVIDED BY THE COPYRIGHT HOLDERS AND CONTRIBUTORS "AS IS" AND * ANY EXPRESS OR IMPLIED WARRANTIES, INCLUDING, BUT NOT LIMITED TO, THE IMPLIED * WARRANTIES OF MERCHANTABILITY AND FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE ARE * DISCLAIMED. IN NO EVENT SHALL THE COPYRIGHT OWNER OR CONTRIBUTORS BE LIABLE FOR * ANY DIRECT, INDIRECT, INCIDENTAL, SPECIAL, EXEMPLARY, OR CONSEQUENTIAL DAMAGES * (INCLUDING, BUT NOT LIMITED TO, PROCUREMENT OF SUBSTITUTE GOODS OR SERVICES; * LOSS OF USE, DATA, OR PROFITS; OR BUSINESS INTERRUPTION) HOWEVER CAUSED AND * ON ANY THEORY OF LIABILITY, WHETHER IN CONTRACT, STRICT LIABILITY, OR TORT * (INCLUDING NEGLIGENCE OR OTHERWISE) ARISING IN ANY WAY OUT OF THE USE OF THIS * SOFTWARE, EVEN IF ADVISED OF THE POSSIBILITY OF SUCH DAMAGE. */ package com.varlamoredistraction; import lombok.AllArgsConstructor; import lombok.Getter; /** * Where a distraction timestamp came from, ordered by how much we trust its precision. *

* {@link #EXACT_LOCAL} is the chat message printing on the tick the distraction begins, so it is * accurate to one tick. {@link #APPROXIMATE_LOCAL} is inferred from a distraction that was already * running when we arrived, which only bounds the start to somewhere in the preceding ~24 seconds. *

* {@link #ESTIMATED_FROM_END} sits between them. Watching a distraction finish and subtracting its * length pins the start to within a couple of seconds - far better than the ~12s of a mid-flight * sighting, but still only as good as the configured duration. It needs its own tier because both * estimates are otherwise equally ranked, and the end-derived stamp is always the earlier of the * two by construction: it subtracts a whole duration where the other subtracts half. Ranking them * on merit rather than letting the earliest-wins rule decide keeps a mis-set duration from making * the worse estimate beat the better one. *

* Precedence only decides between two readings of the same distraction. A newer reading of * a later cycle always wins regardless of source — see {@link DistractionTracker#record}. */ @AllArgsConstructor @Getter enum DistractionSource { EXACT_LOCAL(0, false), ESTIMATED_FROM_END(1, true), APPROXIMATE_LOCAL(2, true); /** Lower is more trusted. */ private final int precedence; /** True if the start was inferred rather than witnessed. Rendered with a leading ~. */ private final boolean approximate; }
